lines: Non-members are always welcome on our trips - please contact the New Members Rep to get put in touch with the trip leader.
Unless otherwise stated, socials are at 110 Waltham Road, Christchurch. Doors open at 7:00 pm with the meeting starting around 7:20 pm and the talk staring at 7:30 pm
moderate - with a bit of off-track navigation
Z (formerly Caltex) Russley Might possibly leave Friday night 7pm or 7am Saturday - talk to leader
POSTPONED - Saturday weather doesn't look good for Saturday Tops camp etc... but will try again!

A trip which aims to get you high on the Coast (legally) and increase your IQ. The plan is to watch the sunset from a high camp on Mt Smart and then on Sunday checkout the historic Smart rock bivy. I believe the club has never been here before. Water would need to be carried for the high campsite. An alternative loop trip, if we have a second vehicle, is a Turiwhate traverse. This also features a high sunset campsite which has a couple of small tarns.

Both trips probably won't encounter snow.. but there could be icy rocks etc... No need for crampons.. but running shoes likely to be inadequate. We will camp at Mitchells if we leave Friday night (club hut in use).
Ice Axe, Crampons, Helmet, Snow Skills
Drive up Mt Olympus access road passed couch corner to first switch back.
Head up road to second switch back then leave the road heading up on the the ridge ~1350m
Head up ridge to pt1783, follow ridge upto pt2096, then you Mt Olympus (2094).
Head south west along ridge to pt1973, then south to pt2009, follow south east ridge down to ~1700m then head down to ski field road and back to car.
Wed 22 July: Wednesday Social Walk #104 – Montgomery Spur
Corner of Rāpaki Road and Centaurus Road 18:30 / 6:30 PM

We will start from the bottom of Rāpaki Road, and follow the track to the Kōwhai Walking Track which runs over Montgomery Spur and back to the Rāpaki Track. Continuing to the Summit Road we’ll take a peek over to the harbour and then take the Mount Vernon Valley Track (a bit of this is off-track) back down to where it meets the Rāpaki Track and follow that back to the start.
About 8.78 KM, 335 metres elevation gain, around 2 hours.
Note that you can claim one Wednesday Social Walk towards the three qualifying trips for club membership.

A chance to break out your finest Christmas jumper as we head into Casey Hut for a Christmas celebration complete with a pot luck feast. Obviously we'll have plenty of sweet treats but please bring something savoury as well even if it's small (cheese, pigs in blankets, leftover turkey curry anything goes). The hut has a long burner and the river isn't too far away (think giant fridge) so feel free to get creative. Games, terrible cracker jokes all welcome.

You will need to book the hut, bookings open on the 12th of May. Even if you're not 100% sure you can make it please book the hut so your booking can be passed down the wait-list if you decide to drop out. I'll send out a reminder the day before bookings open.
If the weather is looking absolutely trash then we will go to the club hut instead so fear not Christmas shall not be derailed.
Will walk in via Casey Saddle 17km and probably out via Binser but open to do what ever people fancy.

A beginner's guide to getting lost and what to do about it, plus some general navigation and bushcraft skills. This is a day of practical training to help prepare you for the day when your planned day walk becomes a potential overnight sleepover. Bring your normal day pack and gear, a good lunch and a sense of humor – some older pre-torn clothes may be useful as the trip does involve some bush bashing. Bring your GPS and/or compass if you have one, but it is not essential because they will be provided for the navigation part of the exercise. We will stop at the Winne Bagoes for tea, a Q&A session and a trip debrief on the way home, because the trip lasts till until 5 - 6pm depending on your navigation skills. This is the only club training course which is open to non-members, and it is designed for trampers looking to step up from easy to moderate trips.

Starting by the shelter at the Upper Cave Stream Reserve, follow the Mistletoe Track through beech forest, then Sidle 73 Track through to the Craigieburn Valley Ski Road. A short section of the ski road and Craigieburn Edge Track takes us up to Lyndon Saddle, from where we ascend Helicopter Hill (1256m). Panoramic views of Castle Hill Basin. The return trip will descend back to Lyndon Saddle, then follow the Luge Track and Broken River Ski Road back to the shelter. Round trip 12kms, 500m height gain.
Z (Caltex) Russell road 6am departure is dependant on which day we climb. If we climb on the Sunday we will leave later
Ice Axe, Crampons, Helmet, Snow Skills, River Crossing
The trip will depend on at least one good weather day to get to the summit.
Plan A: tramp up to east hawdon biv, climb mt valiant and descend back to the biv and camp. Return to the car the next day
Plan B: tramp up to east hawdon biv and camp ( this will be a later start time). Climb mt valiant and then return to the car.
Plan C: tramp to east hawdon biv, climb mt valiant, camp back at the biv. Go out the next day via Smooth peak and the ridge beyond
Which plan we follow will be dependent on weather, conditions and fitness

The route to Mt valiant is alpine grade 1. We head through the scrub across from the stream split past the biv. Then sidle to the saddle between smooth peak and point 1684. Then follow the ridge to the summit. The scrub has a ground trail through it.
Trip is dependent on low avalanche levels and the river being ok.
Time wise I am expecting about 4 hours to the biv and about 4 hours to the summit and back.
It is harder to estimate the time for the second day of plan c but we would set out early and it will be somewhere around 8 hours

Z Rolleston (note - not the usual Z) 7:30am - this means driving off at 7:30am, so please arrive by 7:15am to check in and load the car

Let's go enjoy the awesome views of the snowy tops and golden tussock in the Hakatere, while staying by the lakeside. This is a flat trip but with some decent mileage and multiple lakes/tracks, so it's kind of a double day trip.
We'll drive up to Lake Clearwater, and spend the morning walking the track that circles the lake. Approx 3hrs, 10.5km.
We'll have lunch at a picnic spot, then head to Lake Camp.
We'll spend the afternoon walking from Lake Camp over to Lake Emma, around Lake Emma, and back again. Approx 15km, 4hrs.
The tracks will be very easy indeed, mostly flat tussocky 4wd and maybe a bit muddy. However, this is a day with a fair few km underfoot, hence the easy-mod rating.
Wed 29 July: Pantanal with Andy PrattSocial
Z Russley TBC option for Friday night (let me know earliest) or Saturday morning (snow/ice permitting)
Will add second car if at least 3 on waitlist.
I've always felt the Paparoa wasn't quite long enough to justify a three day weekend so lets try the two day version.

We will most likely stay in the Greymouth TOP10 on Friday night (approx $40pp). Leaving time from Chch tbc depending on when everyone can get away from work. I am also open to the option of leaving Christchurch Saturday morning (6am ish) but that would be dependent on snow/ice forecast. Will finalise nearer the time.

Saturday we will head to the Smokho car park and walk into Moonlight tops hut (approx 20km) hopefully enjoying sunset along the tops. If everyone is keen we could go via Mt Watson as the first section of the Paparoa is a dull plod.

Sunday is a more substantial day at 35km but it is all down hill. Weather permitting I would like to leave the hut pre dawn and walk along the tops a bit for sunrise before stopping for breakfast to avoid disturbing any hut mates but obviously this is weather dependent. So even thought the huts have gas ideally we will have 1 or 2 stoves between us for making the necessary caffeinated beverages.

At this stage the plan is to organise a car relocation (approx $50pp) so the car will be waiting for us when we reach the end of the track (I'm expecting Sunday to take 6-8hrs), then it's the long drive back to Christchurch (approx 4hrs) with a dinner stop along the way.

You will need to book Moonlight Tops Hut as this is a great walk and there is no camping permitted. As Doc's Great Walk Cancellation policy is a bit brutal I suggest we wait until the end of June before booking so we can see how the winter is shaping up.
Sun 9 August: The Symon Winter Adventure 2026 - Heaphy Track East to WestFull
Another Trip inspired by Captain Hann (and FB chats), the Heaphy track in Winter.
Sunday 9th August - meet up and drive over to Takaka, I'm thinking a early morning departure and spending the night somewhere, l'll confirm once we are closer to the date
Monday 10th August- Day one of the Heaphy. We'll drive to the Track end and then walk to Perry Saddle Hut. (AI says 17.5km and around 5 hours)
Tuesday 11th August - Perry Saddle Hut to James Mackay Hut. (AI says 24.2km and 6.5 hours)
Wednesday 12th August- James Mackay Hut to Heaphy Hut (AI says around 6 hours and 20.5km)

Thursday 13th August- Heaphy Hut along the coast to the track end at Kohaihai. It's not a long day (AI says 5 hours/ 16.2km), allowing for travel time and some exploring time then we'll drive back to the club hut in AP to link up with West to East Group and swap cars.

1. We'll be doing a car swap with the East to West Team, the plan is to meet up afterwards at the Club Hut in AP to swap back cars, given the distances and the likelihood that one group may have to wait, I'm thinking we spend the night there.

2. Being a Great Walk, we have to book/ pay to stay in the Huts. Its $30.00 per night (or $19.00 if you want to save $11 per night and camp), bookings open on 20th May so you'll need to get in and book it then.
There will be a Key swap with the West to East Group

Another Trip inspired by Captain Hann (and FB chats), the Heaphy track in Winter.
Sunday 9th August - meet up and drive over to the West Coast, I'm thinking a late morning/ lunchtime departure and spending the night somewhere, l will confirm once we are closer to the date

Monday 10th August- Day one of the Heaphy, we'll drive up to the track end at Kohaihai and walk along the coast to Heaphy Hut. It's not a long day (AI says 5 hours/ 16.2km), allowing for travel time and some exploring time once we get to the Hut
Tuesday 11th August- Heaphy Hut to James Mackay Hut (AI says around 6 hours and 20.5km, but there's some uphill, looks like about 700m of elevation gain)
Wednesday 12th August- James Mackay Hut to Perry Saddle Hut (AI says 24.2km and 6.5 hours)
Thursday 13th August- Perry Saddle Hut to track end (AI says 17.5km and around 4 hours, all downhill!) then we'll drive back to the club hut in AP to link up with East to West Group and swap cars.

Ollie Clifton, South Island Project Manager with BCT, will give an overview of some of the highlights of the 2025/26 summer season with BCT, including a light-hearted insight into some of things which don't always go to plan.
Ollie will also outline plans for the 2026/27 season, & invite feedback & discussion on projects & priorities - your chance to let BCT know what & where it should be focussing it's efforts.
Fri 21 August: The Annual Mueller Hut Pilgrimage Full
Ice Axe, Crampons, Helmet, Avalanche Gear, Snow Skills, Avalanche Training
The Weather Gods seem to be behaving this winter so, after not behaving last year, a trip to Mueller to play in the snow is overdue!
We'll leave after work on Friday, stop at kebab world for dinner and stay the night at Unwin Lodge.

On Saturday, we'll make our way up to Mueller Hut, we'll stop for a second breakfast at Sealy tarns or early Lunch at the Lorraine Poole memorial sinkhole and be at the Hut by early afternoon which gives us time to do a little exploring, either up to Mt Ollivier or wander up towards the Annette ice Plateau.
After an evening enjoying the views and sounds of Avalanches from Mt Sefton, we'll wake up, have breakfast and head back down to the Carpark.
A late lunch will be at the Fairlie Pie shop and we should be home by 4-5pm.
- Distance 5.2km, elevation Gain around 1000m, time between 4 and 5 hours.

- From Sealey tarns to the Ridgeline is considered Complex Avalanche terrain so you need to have some route finding experience, bring avalanche gear and know how it works so this isn't a trip for those who have just done the Snow skills course (sorry).
Sat 29 August: Long Weekend - Copland Track and Hot PoolsFull
Est $170 (fuel + Fri accomm), plus 3 nights DOC hut passes
Z (formerly Caltex) Russley Friday late afternoon - 4:30pm (which means driving at 4:30pm)
A long weekend exploring West Coast forests and rivers, with the bonus of hot pools to soak in at the end of the day.

Welcome Flat hut and campsite must be booked year-round. Once you are registered on the trip you are responsible for booking your own hut or campsite for the 2 nights and confirming your booking to the trip leader - this should be done as soon as possible in case things fill up.
On Friday afternoon we’ll drive down from Christchurch and overnight at a motel in Franz Josef.

Saturday we’ll complete the drive to the carpark and walk the Copland track to Welcome Flat (18km, 500m ascent, 7 hours DOC time), aiming to reach the camping area by late afternoon and get into the hot pools!
Sunday has options: a day trip up the valley to Douglas Rock Hut (7km, 200m ascent, 3 hours DOC time, rougher track), or a more relaxed day based at the campsite for those keen to take it easy.
On Monday we’ll make an early start for the decent walk out and the long drive back to Christchurch.
Come prepared for river crossings and sandflies, and winter weather.
Tramping will be at a chilled/relaxed/fairly slow pace although we will still move steadily. I'm not a fast tramper, so if you are, please only sign up if you are prepared to remain with the group.
This trip is weather dependent and may be cancelled or rescheduled if conditions are unsuitable.
Please note: I will be asking new joiners to contribute an upfront $70 deposit to cover non-refundable Friday night accommodation already paid for.

Sat 29 August: The Annual Winter Games weekendFull
Time for another Games weekend at the CTC Hut in Arthurs Pass!
We'll head on up to the Club Hut, play some boardgames, maybe sit quietly and read a book, eat some food and go for a short walk (to at least have a fig leaf of respectability as a tramping trip!)
Want to yell out "you sunk my battleship!", like how pretty the Azul tiles look, the thought of Bananagrams excites you... then this is for you!

Fri 11 September: Jim and James' Winter Trip - Angelus HutFull
Z (formerly Caltex) Russley Leaving Friday Lunchtime 1pm
Ice Axe, Crampons, Helmet, Avalanche Gear, Snow Skills

Angelus Hut has been on our radar for some time! We will leave early afternoon on Friday (around 1pm departure) for the drive up to Nelson Lakes, once at the Mt Robert Carpark we will head up to Speargrass hut for the night. It’s an easy 2 hour walk in the dark on a well-formed track, giving us more time on Saturday to sleep in / explore around Angelus Hut, or potentially head up Mt Angelus.

On Saturday, we will head up the Speargrass Route to Angelus Hut, it's not as scenic as Robert ridge but it is also relatively sheltered and not a hard slog. We will be at Angelus Hut reasonably early (around/ just after Lunch) so can spend the afternoon exploring, climbing some nearby hills/ peaks or relax in the hut by the fire.

On Sunday we will head back down to the Cars along the Robert Ridge route (weather permitting), with some great alpine views along the way. We should be back at the car in the early afternoon and start the trip back home.
Travel times/ walking times (based on last time):
• Christchurch to Mt Robert Carpark – approximately 5 hours
• Carpark to Speargrass Hut – 2 hours, Cumulative Elevation gain 180m (around 300m if you count down and up!)
• Speargrass Hut to Angelus Hut – around 4-5 hours, around 700m of elevation gain
• Angelus Hut to Mt Robert Carpark along Robert Ridge (5-6 Hours), a bit of up and a lot of down elevation wise.

• Ice Axe, Crampons, Helmet and Avalanche gear (and skills, knowledge of how to use them) are essential. If you do not have these, you can hire from the club, note that there are only 4 Avalanche Sets so you'll need to be quick, you can also hire kits from Bivouac and Further Faster (I think)
• Angelus Hut is booked! I’ve booked 8 spaces at the hut to make sure we don’t miss out. The hut cost is $32 and I will add this to your bill at the end.
Sat 12 September: Casey Hut via Poulter River Track - flat trip!Full
Z Rolleston (note different departure point) 8am (this means driving off at 8am, please arrive by 7:45 to load the car)
I'm all about the flat trips this winter. Let's go to Casey Hut!
We'll be taking the Poulter River track from Mt White Rd up to the hut.
This is not the usual Casey/Binser circuit, but a track following the adjacent Poulter river.
18km one way, undulations but no climbs, expecting lots of nice views of snowy tops and the wintry river.
While it should be an easy trip, it goes nice and deep into Arthurs Pass National Park.
Pack warmly in case there's no firewood.
I don't do walking in snow, so if there's a blizzard down to river level or otherwise dangerous weather conditions, we'll reschedule.
Our pace will be quite slow and relaxed, so please only sign up if you're prepared to remain with the group. I'm not a fast tramper. And this trip is about enjoyment and active relaxation.
Casey Hut must be booked if you want to stay inside (yes, even at this time of year), or camp outside at your choice.
Even if you have an annual hut pass, you still need to book, but it will be no cost to you.
Please confirm which one is you to the trip leader on registering.
You're responsible for arranging your own hut booking.
Come along to find out about the club's Youth Programme

This evening is a great opportunity for anyone considering becoming a trip leader, interested in doing so at a future date or looking to refresh their trip-leading knowledge and skills. We'll explain everything from deciding where to go, right through to calculating the transport cost at the end of the trip, and everything in between. If you intend on leading just one trip a year, or doing it regularly, this course will put you on the right track to get started.

If you've ever wanted to tramp in a particular area but don't have people to go with, being a trip leader is an excellent way of making it happen and having a social group to join you. You get to decide the location, route, speed, maximum numbers etc.
Please sign up if you intend on attending.
Sun 11 October: The Summit Road Emu Parade
Do you remember doing the Emu Parade at School or in Cubs? If not, an Emu Parade is where everyone lines up and moves across a field picking up Rubbish.

I've decided to indulge my nostalgia for Emu Parades and cleaning up obsession by picking up Rubbish on the Summit Road, and since the CTC are quite often using the Summit Road for trips (many of you will have a love-hate relationship due to the Diamond Harbour to Lyttelton walk), it's a good opportunity to show an appreciation for it by making it a little tidier.
The Plan is to spend a few hours picking up Rubbish, the Summit Road Society have indicated a section of the road that needs a bit of Aroha.
2. A stick or walking pole (or something like that) to help pick up stuff
1. Rubbish Bags and a trailer to take rubbish to a transfer station.
2. Hand Sanitiser/ Soap and other stuff to make you feel clean during/ after
So come on, let's show some love of the Summit Road and tidy up a small bit of it!

Wed 21 October: Mark's Cookery Competition- MasterChef version 2.0Social
Since last years MasterChef Cooking competition was such as success, let's do it again!
I'm going to change it up a little this year, there are going to be three categories:
1. Vegetarian/ Vegan - since we have quite a few Vegetarians/ Vegans in the club, create a vegetable based culinary extravaganza
2. A Sweet treat- who doesn't like a treat after a hard day!? create a special something to excite the taste buds
3. Pimped up Dehy- have a special ingredient (or ingredients) that turns Dehy into Delicious? wow us
The rules (pretty much the same as last year):
- Maximum weight of ingredients (excluding Cooker, utensils etc) = 500gms (I have a scale this year!)
- You can do pre-prep of ingredients
- You can't use the Meeting room kitchen except to get water
- Non-perishable food only (so no raw meat or fresh Milk)
- 25 minutes to cook and present, then 10 minutes for the rest of us to taste
- It can be entree/ main or dessert
- For the Dehy, can be any pre-packaged meal.
- Have the recipe and ingredients handy, as we may want to try out making ourselves (like last year, I'll put them on the CTC FB page afterwards).
A winner for each category will be decided by all in a popular vote, and like last year, there will be prizes, maybe some trophies.
Not prepared to be a MasterChef but fancy yourself as a master food critic? come along and taste some yummy food then vote on the best.
Wed 4 November: Nepal mini series part 1: Where the mountains reach the sky - with Carol ArmstrongSocial

Carol has travelled to Nepal 6 times, during the 1990s and more recently in 2023 and 2026 . From wild water rafting, visiting Chitwan NP to the endless stunningly beautiful trails throughout the Everest Region and Annapurna region. This time our footsteps took us to Gokyo Lakes and over Renjo La Pass @ 5345m Photos and thoughts from our trip to Gokyo Lakes and may be a few from EBC in 2023. Q&A welcome - from choosing a guide / trekking agency, challenges of walking at altitude, fitness, etc ....
Wed 18 November: Nepal mini series part 2, The Highs and the Lows: Tramping in the Himalayas with Sushil PoudelSocial

Are you curious about how tramping culture is evolving in the small Himalayan country of Nepal? Once enjoyed solely by international visitors, the trekking trails are now seeing a growing number of young local adventurers. Before moving to New Zealand, I used to lead tramping trips in Nepal. Join me for a talk exploring the highs and lows of trekking in the Himalayas, the changing outdoor culture in Nepal, sustainability of mountain tourism and some insights from my personal experiences on the trails.

Thu 17 December: Ice Lake Revenge - New Dates Part 2Full
Moderate/Hard but at a Moderate Pace
Z (formerly Caltex) Russley 6 pm on Thursday, 17 December

Please note that the dates for this trip are subject to change as it is very weather-dependent. If bad weather presents itself, I will not cancel this trip, only reschedule for a later date. We will also consider adding one other car if we manage to garner interest.
Also note: Last year, we never got to Ice Lake because of how high the river was to cross the top branch of the Butler. This year, we are coming back for revenge!
We will leave Christchurch around 6 pm on Thursday with a plan to overnight in Arthur’s Pass at the club hut.

The next morning, we will have an early start (in the car by 4 AM!) with the goal of reaching Whataroa as early as possible to start tramping (should be around 7 AM). About 5ks out of Whataroa, we will find the trailhead. After parking the car, we will head up the valley. Should be a relatively easy 7.5ks to the Perth River Junction (2 hours). From there, the track gets a bit more exciting. According to DOC, this should take around 7 hours to get up to Top Butler Hut (but last year it took us 10).

The aim is to stop at Top Butler Hut for the night! What does this mean for you? Well, epic views and a decent hut and... a full 12 to 13 hours of tramping on day one. I know it sounds crazy, but it is doable!

This year, I will be watching the weather like crazy to find a long dry spell to make sure that we will, in fact, be able to cross the top branch of the Butler! Once we have done so, we will rejoice and then head off up the last 2 hours of track (with our track record - pun intended - it will probably take around 4 hours). Either way, we should have a full day in which we make our attempt to reach Ice Lake. Depending on when we do so, we will try to get a fair bit of the way out before we camp for the night (probably somewhere along the track like we did last year).
We finish whatever we didn't do yesterday and then start the long drive back, victorious, knowing that Ice Lake did not beat us again.
7.3km from the carpark to Perth River Track Junction (2 hours)
9.06km from Perth River Track Junction to Butler Junction Hut (6 hours)
5.81km Butler Junction Hut to Ice Lake (~6 hours. 4 hours to Top Butler Hut and 2 hours (?) to the lake)
Important things to keep in mind:
- Please bring a tent. The huts are not bookable, and we don’t want to be forced to overnight at huts due to one person not bringing a tent.
- These will be very long days (but worthwhile!). Be sure that you are ready for 12+ hours of West Coast tramping with a full pack!

- Our pace is steady, but NOT FAST. Trey has type-1 diabetes and we need to stop regularly to check his blood sugar levels. If you are keen to go with us, please come prepared for moderate tramping with frequent stops. I won't allow our group to split up, so if you are fast, please come with patience.
- For those who are keen (and faster than we are), I will bring some tools to help clear some track while you wait for us to catch up.
Tue 22 December: A Very Mark Christmas - George SoundFull
I liked it so much the first time, I am going to go back, this time for Christmas!
22nd December - drive down from Christchurch and stay (camp?) somewhere close to Te Anau Downs so we can be at the Boat ramp nice and early.
23rd December - catch the boat across Lake Te Anau and up Middle Arm, portage to Lake Hankinson and get dropped off, then it's a 2-3 hour walk to Thompson Hut

24th December - A BIG DAY, walk up and over Henry Pass, then down to Lake Katherine, around Lake Katherine and down to the Hut at George Sound. while it is around 10km distance, it will likely take 10-12 hours as it is slow going!

25th December - Spend a cruisy Christmas Day at George Sound - Eating/ exploring/ Swimming etc (weather permitting of course!), last year I carried a rock melon, maybe this year I'll carry something christmassy!
26th December - time to come back, but this time stopping at Henry Pass to camp and hopefully climb some nearby peaks.
27th December - Walk back to Hankinson Hut

28th December - Spend a chilled day at the Hut before getting picked up by the boat and, depending on pick up time, drive some of the way home (not likely to be very far as Boat pick up is around 5pm).
I am open to continuing the fun with another trip in Fiordland if options arise and people are open (i.e. one car could come back and one car stay down there)
